help.source: The oldest segments are evicted when the cache reaches this size.
Warms the opening of the next episode so it starts instantly.
Fraction of the current episode watched (0–1).
How much of the next episode to pull ahead.
Keeps the resume point of unfinished titles cached.
An unfinished title nobody has watched for this long loses its cache pin. Empty uses 30 days.

help.source: Percent of the disk budget unfinished titles may keep pinned; the least recently watched lose their pin first. 0 uses 50.

Two-letter region for release dates and streaming availability.

description.source: Hide obscure titles from libraries. They stay searchable.

help.source: Hide automatic franchise groups, such as Zootopia.

description.source: Extra copies of the same picture, after Auto.

help.source: Listed after Auto in the app's version menu.
Apply the alternatives count to each available resolution, up to seven versions total. Auto stays first; profile and device limits still apply.
Version menus can list releases taller than the profile. Off keeps the ceiling you set. HDR and file-size limits still apply.

description.source: How many releases Ether keeps ready, and how long it remembers a search. The defaults are enough for a household.

help.source: Fallback releases kept for instant failover.
Articles checked before a release is trusted.

description.source: Blocked terms match whole tokens. sub matches SUB, not Subtitles or SUBPACK. Subtitle language tags alone do not prove burned-in subtitles.

help.source: Video checks run after playback starts. A newly discovered verdict applies to later selections.

description.source: Ether plays the file directly when the app can. It converts the video on this computer only when it has to.

help.source: Automatic uses this computer's graphics chip when an app can't play the file as-is. Choose Off only if converted video looks wrong.
Linux graphics device, for example /dev/dri/renderD128. Leave empty unless converted video fails to start.
How many videos can be converted at once. Leave the default unless several people watch together and the computer struggles.
Limits picture quality for people watching away from home, so the stream fits their connection. 0 means no limit.

description.source: On a supported NVIDIA graphics card, Ether can clean up a soft video before sending it. This uses extra graphics power, and Ether installs what it needs on a supported Windows computer.

help.source: Cleans up a soft picture before it is sent. The viewer's resolution and bitrate limits still apply. Unsupported videos play normally.
Videos taller than this play normally, without enhancement.
The tallest picture enhancement is allowed to produce.
Higher quality uses more of the graphics card. Streaming choices need a recent NVIDIA card. Medium is a good start.
Additional streams play normally once this many are already being enhanced.
Leave empty and Ether sets this up itself. A path you fill in is never replaced.

description.source: Ether includes the programs it needs. Change a path only if you installed your own copy.

help.source: Leave empty to use the bundled ffmpeg.
Leave empty to use the program Ether includes.
Where converted video is written while it plays. Empty uses the normal temporary folder.

description.source: Sync watch history and lists with Trakt.
Fetch subtitles when a release doesn't include them.

help.source: When a viewer's subtitle setting asks for subtitles and none in their language is available, Ether downloads one once the video starts playing. Uses one OpenSubtitles download per title per viewer, so standard accounts may run out sooner.

label.source: Download a subtitle automatically when playback starts

help.source: Checks the signed release feed every few hours.
Installs during the maintenance window, once nobody is watching.
24-hour local time.
May wrap past midnight.
Leave empty for the official feed.
How long a clustered node waits for current playback to end before installing. Leave empty to wait 30 minutes. A server on its own waits until nobody is watching.

title.source: Test playback with a local file

label.source: Look up intro and credits markers

help.source: Only use torrents your debrid service already holds. Nothing is downloaded and playback never waits. Turn off to have Ether send the best uncached release of a title to your first debrid service when someone presses Play; it plays once the download finishes (the app says so meanwhile).
Remove torrents Ether added that turned out not to be cached. Cached torrents stay on your account so the next play starts instantly and they are reused instead of re-added.

description.source: Leave at 0 for the built-in behaviour.

help.source: Requests start at 512 KiB for a fast first byte and grow up to this size. 0 = 8 MiB; at most 64 MiB.
0 adapts read-ahead to the measured download speed. Set up to 32 chunks to fix the window; -1 turns read-ahead off.
Concurrent range requests per open file. 0 = 4; at most 16.

description.source: Lets Plex apps save titles for offline viewing. Ether remuxes each one on demand.

help.source: Off lets only you download. A viewer's access policy can still allow or deny it.
Downloads are capped at this resolution. 0 uses 1080p.
Across the whole server. 0 uses 2.
0 uses 1.
Maximum space for prepared downloads. Set to 0 to use the default limit of 20 GiB.
A finished download is deleted after this long if the app hasn't fetched it.

description.source: Extras for each viewer. Turn any off for the plain layout.
